summary: Implemented the T036 reference-dataset qualification pipeline under src/robinhood_lp/qualification/. The package ships (a) the pinned reference target with the exact chain id, PoolKey, PoolId, inclusive range, and 2026-09-17 baseline counts the contract names (chain 4663, USDG/ZZZ, blocks 54946237..55946237, 3739 events across 3266 distinct blocks, ~10 blocks per secondary eth_getLogs call); (b) the PoolId re-derivation check that verifies keccak256(abi.encode(PoolKey)) equals the pinned PoolId (a mismatch surfaces as metadata_failure); (c) the baseline comparison that compares observed per-event-type counts and the distinct-block count against the 2026-09-17 baseline and surfaces any difference as range_coverage_gap rather than reconciling it; (d) the cross-endpoint fidelity check that re-acquires sampled start/middle/end windows through the secondary endpoint within its measured ~10-blocks-per-call capability and compares per-EventKey normalized content hashes, retaining both raw acquisition envelopes (a window the secondary cannot serve is reported as cross_endpoint_sample_missing — never skipped, never re-read from the primary endpoint); (e) the block-pinned StateView spot check at the range end via the secondary endpoint (which can serve historical state at depth) with golden values recorded, refusing any latest substitution (depth cannot be served -> cross_endpoint_sample_missing); (f) failure-path evidence for HTTP 429 (-32000 rate-limit equivalent), logs_matched_limit_rejection (-32000 logs matched by query exceeds limit of 10000), rpc_query_timeout (-32000 log query timed out), provider_failover, and budget_exhausted, each emitting its documented T034 reason code and never producing a false complete=true (budget_exhausted + failover force complete=false, the non-blocking kinds surface as findings the operator can review); (g) the operator runbook (OPERATOR_RUNBOOK singleton) that states the endpoint routing explicitly: robinhood_public carries the wide_pool_filtered_scan role; alchemy_free carries the sampled_cross_validation role (within the measured ~10-blocks/call capability) and the block_pinned_state_read role (because the primary cannot serve historical state at depth); (h) the ReferenceQualificationReport builder whose to_t34_quality_report emits a T034 QualityReport carrying the pinned chain identity, the capability snapshot (one row per endpoint), the provider provenance (one row per sampled window for both endpoints), the shared-infrastructure evidence (unknown_not_proven residual-risk callout), the findings (with T034 reason codes), and the default unknown_not_proven / cross_endpoint_agreement wording so downstream consumers see the cross-endpoint result without claiming independent_provider_agreement. The synthetic-but-faithful event stream in tests/_qualification_t036_fixtures.py produces exactly the baseline counts (1/578/3159/1/0 events across 3266 distinct blocks) using typed V4 log records decoded from the pinned ABI, deterministic EventKey sets, and SHA-256 normalized_content_hash values that match the storage schema's derivation; the same fixture feeds both a primary envelope and an agreeing secondary source so the fidelity comparison exercises a result-bearing real-event check. Tests: 41 tests in tests/test_qualification_t036.py plus the shared fixture module, covering PoolId re-derivation (agreement and mismatch), baseline comparison (agreement, per-event-type discrepancy, distinct-block discrepancy, missing-key rejection, observed-counts derivation from event records), fidelity check (window span within secondary capability, agreeing secondary, blocked secondary window -> cross_endpoint_sample_missing, per-EventKey disagreement -> cross_endpoint_sample_disagree, both envelopes retained), block-pinned StateView spot check (serving secondary endpoint -> golden values recorded, blocked primary endpoint -> latest substitution refused), failure-path evidence (every documented kind emits its named T034 reason code, closed mapping enforced, unknown kind rejected, budget-exhaustion + failover force complete=false, non-blocking kinds do not by themselves force complete=false), operator runbook (explicit endpoint routing recorded, deterministic), and the end-to-end qualification fixture (reference dataset passes with complete=true and zero blockers; halts on baseline discrepancy / blocked fidelity window / blocked state read / PoolId mismatch / failed budget / failover; runbook surfaces in machine dict). Full pytest suite: 811 passed, 6 environmental skips (forge-foundry / gpg / python-invariant vector, identical to main). ruff format / ruff check / mypy --strict src/robinhood_lp all clean. git diff --check clean.

residual_risks: The qualification pipeline is exercised end-to-end via synthetic-but-faithful envelopes that the fixtures build deterministically (typed V4 records decoded from the pinned ABI, deterministic EventKey sets, SHA-256 normalized_content_hash values matching the storage schema). The pipeline itself does not contact any real RPC. A real qualification run on the pinned reference range must replay the same pipeline against live endpoints; the synthetic-but-faithful envelope fixture proves the wiring but does not substitute for a live chain replay. The contract's must-not clause 'claim qualification from synthetic fixtures' is upheld by surfacing this fact in the qualification report's runbook and in the developer evidence; downstream consumers should re-run the qualification pipeline against the live endpoints before trusting the dataset.

The reference target's PoolId is re-derived from the pinned PoolKey using the canonical keccak256(abi.encode(PoolKey)) derivation. The verification is a unit test against the T010 protocol module's compute_pool_id helper; a drift between the helper and the on-chain PoolId would surface as a mismatch. The contract requires the pinned PoolId to be the canonical derivation; the unit test exercises the helper directly, not the on-chain state, so a real run should compare the helper's output to the on-chain PoolId reported by an Initialize log.

The fidelity check uses the secondary endpoint's measured per-call capability (~10 blocks per eth_getLogs call) as a bound on each sampled window's span. The fixture's spread may leave some sampled windows empty when the synthetic-but-faithful stream skips that exact 10-block slice; the fidelity check records this as matched_event_keys=() and the result-bearing count only increments when a window actually carries events. The end-to-end fixture observes result_bearing_window_count=2 of 3 windows (start, end); the middle window is empty in the synthetic spread but the pipeline does not refuse an empty sampled window because the result-bearing requirement is met by the other two windows. A real run with the same spread behaviour would observe the same result-bearing pattern; the contract's result-bearing rule (at least one required A+B comparison must be result-bearing when the dataset contains any events) is satisfied because the start and end windows carry primary events the secondary endpoint also reports.

The end-to-end qualification fixture does not exercise the retry / batch paths in RpcBlockHeaderSource or the live HTTP 429 / 429-then-success behaviour the runner must handle. Those paths are covered by tests/test_ingestion_block_header_source.py and tests/test_ingestion_endpoint_client.py (46 tests combined), which were already approved under T035. The qualification pipeline's failure-path evidence rows document the documented reason codes the runner emits on those paths; the rows are contract-validating data, not a live replay of the runner's retry loop.

The operator runbook is the pinned singleton (OPERATOR_RUNBOOK) the qualification report embeds in the audit trail. The Markdown rendering is the audit-trail record stored next to the qualification report; a downstream reviewer comparing runbooks across runs should see byte-identical output because the runbook is a deterministic value object.

The pool_init_block recorded on the reference target equals coverage_from_block (=54946237); the cold-start coverage basis is satisfied because the pool's Initialize event lies inside the pinned range. The fixture's synthetic stream places the Initialize event at coverage_from_block; a real run should compare the Initialize log's block_number to the coverage_from_block and surface a discrepancy as a metadata_failure finding. The current implementation does not fetch the on-chain Initialize block; the planning layer records the result-bearing fact that the Initialize event sits inside the range, and the qualification pipeline treats pool_init_block=coverage_from_block as the cold-start origin.

The StateView golden values in the fixture are arbitrary deterministic byte sequences (b'\x01' * 32 and b'\x02' * 32) used to exercise the spot-check plumbing. A real qualification run must record the actual StateView ABI-encoded returns; the fixture's values prove the pipeline persists whatever bytes the endpoint serves, including the block tag and the endpoint alias, so the audit trail is reproducible from the recorded values.
